metadata.case_name: CHAN TO WAI v. RIGID PLUMBING LTD. AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.education_level: Certificate in Plumbing and Pipefitting (Apprentices) in 1985

injuries.description: Rupture of right eyeball leading to total blindness and removal of right eye
source: At about 2:10 p.m. on 14 September 1990, the Plaintiff ... the grinding plate or disc of the cutting machine suddenly broke, causing fragments to enter the Plaintiff's right eye.
He was admitted to the United Christian Hospital and was found to suffer a rupture of his right eyeball which was repaired surgically under general anaesthesia.
His right eye later became totally blind and had to be removed.
He underwent a number of surgical operations and had his right eyeball removed seven months after the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: Schizophrenia (psychiatric disorder) developing after the accident
source: Within a few months of the accident, the Plaintiff showed mental symptoms which developed into schizophrenia.
I find, on balance of probabilities, that it is more probable than not that the mental illness of the Plaintiff was caused by and the result of the accident.

manifestations.description: Bleeding of right eye immediately after injury

treatments_received: right eyeball removed seven months after the accident
treatment at public hospitals or clinics
treatments_future: new prosthesis fitted once every 6 to 8 years
visits to an Ophthalmologist 2 to 3 times a year

losses.description: Loss of right eye and total blindness
Serious mental disability (schizophrenia) resulting in gross disability
